He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]]. ==Early life== Gary is the son of Roxanne Holt and [[Gary Trent]], an American former professional basketball player. He has three brothers named Garyson, Grayson and Graydon. Gary's father, Gary Trent Sr., played on the 1993 U.S. Olympic Festival North Team that finished with a 4–0 record and captured the gold medal. He also played basketball at Ohio University, nine years in the NBA for the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], [[Toronto Raptors]], [[Milwaukee Bucks]], [[Dallas Mavericks]] and [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] and also competed in Greece and Italy.{{cite web| url = https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/t/trent-jr-gary-1.aspx| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160611100722/http://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/t/trent-jr-gary-1.aspx| url-status = dead| archive-date = June 11, 2016| title = Gary Trent Jr.}} Trent Jr. first attended [[Apple Valley High School (South California)|Apple Valley High School]] in [[Apple Valley, Minnesota]]. As a sophomore, he averaged 21.5 points per game. As a junior, he averaged 26.4 points per game and 5.8 rebounds per game, while earning Gatorade Minnesota Player of the Year, first-team Minneapolis All Metro honors, in addition to being named a first-team junior All-American by Maxpreps.{{Cite web|url=https://usatodayhss.com/2016/gatorade-minnesota-boys-basketball//amp|title=Minnesota Boys Basketball POY: Gary Trent Jr|date=March 17, 2016|publisher=USA Today High School Sports|access-date=December 26, 2020}}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} Trent Jr. Averaged 22.2 points per game on the web|url=https://usatodayhss.com/2016/five-star-wing-gary-trent-jr-and-the-panthers-are-the-best-team-in-the-nike-eybl-apple-valley-tre-jones/amp|title=Five-star wing Gary Trent Jr and the Panthers are unbeaten in the competitive Nike EYBL|last=Jordan|first=Jason|date=May 14, 2016|publisher=USA Today High School Sports|access-date=December 26, 2020}}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 Prep|last=Lykins|first=Chad|date=August 29, 2016|work=[[CBS Sports]]|access-date=April 24, 2020}} As a senior, he averaged 31.8 points, 6.4 rebounds and 3.8 assist per game while leading his team to a 29–3 overall record.{{Cite web|url=https://andscape.com/features/duke-bound-gary-trent-jr-nba-father-gary-trent-sr/amp/|title=Duke–bound Gary Trent Jr has been schooled by his father on and off the selected to play in both 2017 [[Jordan Brand Classic]] and [[2017 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]]. ===Recruiting=== Trent Jr. was rated as a five-star recruit and considered one of the best overall = #12 | rivals overall = #13 | 247 overall = #10 | espn overall = #8 | accessdate = September 6, 2016 | bball = yes }} ==College career== Trent Jr. signed his letter of intent to attend [[Duke University]] on November 10, 2016. His Duke entering class included 7 highly rated recruits, four of whom were—like Trent—rated to be 5-star players. The group was the consensus top-rated entering class in the country.{{cite web|last1=Solari|first1=Chris|title=Michigan State basketball target Gary Trent Jr. picks Duke|url=http://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/michigan-state/spartans/2016/11/10/michigan-state-basketball-gary-trent-jr/93621550/|website=Detroit Free Press|access-date=August 22, 2017|date=November 10, 2016}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/video/clip/_/id/18018166|title=Trent Jr couldn't turn down playing for Coach K – ESPN Video|date=November 11, 2016 |access-date=April 3, 2023}} Entering the season, despite starting four freshmen, Duke was the preseason number 1 team and stayed within the top ten throughout the season. Trent had multiple highlights during the season. On December 9, 2017, Trent Jr. scored 25 points in an 89–84 loss against [[Boston College Eagles|Boston College]], where he also tied the Duke Freshman record for six three point shots made. On January 13, 2018, despite battling an illness, Trent scored 19 points in a victory over [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400986198|title=Without a sick Coach K, No.7 Duke beats Wake Forest 89–71|website=ESPN.com|access-date=January 13, 2018}} Against [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami]] on January 15, Trent scored a career-high 30 points in a Duke comeback victory.{{cite news|last1=Alexander|first1=Jonathan|title=If there's one thing for certain, it's that Duke's Gary Trent Jr. has shown he is clutch|url=http://www.newsobserver.com/sports/college/acc/duke/duke-now/article195615694.html|access-date=January 24, 2018|work=The News & Observer|date=January 19, 2018}} On January 22, 2018, Trent was named [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] Co-Player and Rookie of the week.{{Cite web|url=https://theacc.com/news/2018/1/22/mens-basketball-acc-announces-basketball-players-of-the-week.aspx|title=ACC Announces Basketball Players of the Week|website=theacc.com|date=January 22, 2018 |publisher=[[Atlantic Coast Conference]]|access-date=January 22, 2018}} On January 29, 2018, he scored a double-double of 22 points 10 rebounds in an 88–66 victory against [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|Notre Dame]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400986231|title=Trent, No.4 Duke bounce back by routing Irish 88–66|website=ESPN.com|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|access-date=January 29, 2018}} Duke entered the [[2018 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] as the No. 2 seed. After beating Notre Dame in the first round, Duke lost in the semi-finals against rival [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]]. Duke entered the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2018 NCAA men's basketball tournament]] as the #2 seed in the Midwest. In the tournament, the Duke team defeated the [[2017–18 Iona Gaels men's basketball team|Iona]], [[2017–18 Rhode Island Rams men's basketball team|Rhode Island]], and [[2017–18 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]], thereby advancing to the 4th round. In the Elite Eight, they lost to [[2017–18 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]] in overtime. Afterward, all five Duke starters announced they would pursue a career in professional basketball. These included one senior, [[Grayson Allen]], and four freshmen: Trent, along with teammates [[Marvin Bagley III]], [[Wendell Carter, Jr]], and [[Trevon Duval]].{{cite web|url=https://goduke.com/news/2018/4/7/211709757.aspx#:~:text=DURHAM%2C%20N.C.%20%E2%80%93%20Duke%20freshman%20guard,declare%20for%20the%20NBA%20Draft.|title=Gary Trent, Jr. Declares for NBA Draft|date=April 7, 2018|website=[[Duke Blue Devils]]|access-date=April 3, 2023}} ==Professional career== ===Portland Trail Blazers (2018–2021)=== [[File:Gary Trent Jr (cropped).jpg|thumb|Trent with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in 2019]] On June 21, 2018, Trent Jr. was drafted by the [[Sacramento Kings]] with the 37th overall selection in the [[2018 NBA draft]]. He was subsequently traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-acquire-draft-rights-gary-trent-jr|title=TRAIL BLAZERS ACQUIRE DRAFT RIGHTS TO GARY TRENT JR.|work=TrailBlazers.com|date=June 21, 2018|access-date=June 21, 2018}} Trent Jr. signed with the Trail Blazers to a three-year deal on July 6.{{cite web |title=Portland signs rookie Gary Trent Jr. to 3-year deal |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/usa/nba/280623/portland-signs-rookie-gary-trent-jr-to-3-year-deal.html |website=Sportando |access-date=July 6, 2018 }}{{Dead link|date=December 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} During his rookie year, Trent played in 15 NBA games, averaging 2.7 points per game. Much of the season, the Blazers assigned him to the [[Texas Legends]] for an [[NBA G League]].{{cite web |title=Portland Trail Blazers Assign Anfernee Simons and Gary Trent Jr to G-League |url=https://ripcityproject.com/2019/01/20/portland-trail-blazers-assign-anfernee-simons-gary-trent-jr-g-league/ |website=[[FanSided]] |date=January 20, 2019 |access-date=January 27, 2019 |archive-date=January 30, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220130121231/https://ripcityproject.com/2019/01/20/portland-trail-blazers-assign-anfernee-simons-gary-trent-jr-g-league/ |url-status=dead }} During his 2nd and 3rd years in the NBA, Trent's numbers significantly improved. He averaged 22 minutes and 8.9 points per game in the 2019–2020 season and 31 minutes and 15 points per game during his 3rd season.{{cite web | url=https://www.nba.com/stats/player/1629018 | title=Gary Trent Jr. | Toronto Raptors | website=[[NBA.com]] }} ===Toronto Raptors (2021–2024)=== On March 25, 2021, the [[Toronto Raptors]] acquired Trent Jr. and [[Rodney Hood]] in a trade for [[Norman Powell]].{{Cite web|title=Raptors Acquire Trent Jr. and Hood from Portland|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/raptors-acquire-trent-jr-and-hood-portland|access-date=2021-03-25|website=NBA.com|language=en}} Trent Jr. scored a then career-high 31 points in a March 31 loss to the Oklahoma City Thunder.{{Cite web|title=Gary Trent Jr.'s career night not enough as Toronto Raptors fall to Oklahoma City Thunder|url=https://ca.nba.com/news/gary-trent-jrs-career-night-not-enough-as-toronto-raptors-fall-to-oklahoma-city-thunder/1nvrhiionozfl12ghwdm15kmqt|access-date=2021-04-01|website=NBA.com Canada {{!}} The official site of the NBA|language=en}} On April 2, in a 53-points blowout win over the [[Golden State Warriors]], Trent Jr. recorded the second-highest [[plus–minus (sports)|plus–minus]] (+54) since the league started tracking the stat in 1996.{{Cite web|last1=Ch|first1=Michael J.|last2=ler|title=Raptors set franchise record with 53-point win over Warriors|url=https://www.thescore.com/nba/news/2141800|access-date=2021-04-11|website=theScore.com|date=April 3, 2021 }} On April 10, he scored a career-high 44 points on 17 of 19 shooting in a 135–115 victory over the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{Cite web|last=Rose|first=Aaron|title=Gary Trent Jr.'s Career Night Leads Raptors to Surprising Victory|url=https://www.si.com/nba/raptors/news/toronto-raptors-get-career-performance-from-gary-trent-jr-in-win-over-cavaliers|access-date=2021-04-11|website=Sports Illustrated|date=April 10, 2021 |language=en}} On August 2, 2021, Trent Jr. signed a three-year, $54 million deal with the Raptors.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31944650/sources-toronto-raptors-gary-trent-jr-agree-3-year-54-million-deal|title=Sources: Toronto Raptors, Gary Trent Jr. agree to 3-year, $54 million deal|website=ESPN.com|last=Bontemps|first=Tim|date=August 3, 2021|access-date=December 11, 2021}} On January 25, 2022, Trent Jr. scored 32 points in a 125–113 win vs the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{Cite On July 20, 2024, Trent Jr. signed a one-year minimum deal with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks Sign Gary Trent Jr.|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-sign-gary-trent-jr|website=NBA.com|date=July 20, 2024|access-date=July 20, 2024}} On February 9, 2025, Trent Jr. scored a then season-high 23 points during a win over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web |title=Lillard leads the way as Bucks beat 76ers 135-127 without Antetokounmpo |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401705320 |website=ESPN.com |publisher=ESPN |language=en}} On April 10, Trent Jr. scored a season–high 29 points during a 111-107 win over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite web |agency=Associated Press | the [[Indiana Pacers]], Trent scored 37 points, including nine three-pointers, in a 117–101 victory. His nine three-pointers tied a playoff record in Bucks franchise history.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401768048|title=Trent ties Bucks playoff mark with 9 3s, he and Giannis score 37 in 117-101 Game 3 win over Pacers|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=April 26, 2025|access-date=April 26, 2025}} The Bucks were eliminated in five games, despite Trent's 33-point performance in a 119–118 closeout overtime loss in Game 5.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401768050|title=Haliburton and Pacers eliminate Bucks from playoffs, closing OT with 8-0 run to win 119-118|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=April 29, 2025|access-date=May 10, 2025}} On July 8, 2025, Trent Jr. re–signed with the Bucks on a two-year, $7.5 million contract.
